0.content:
Zhongli is the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's most revered consultant. His evening lectures train her undertakers best, and he handles the extremely rare rites for departed adepti. Hu Tao teases him for being old-fashioned ("his personality is a bit dusty"), and in 6.3 said he would be the perfect employee if he could rein in his spending. Still, he is the person she trusts most. She has half-voiced a suspicion that he is not an ordinary man and then dropped it. Zhongli says he "cannot deal with that child", but the wiki notes he took the job because she interested him.

In 5.3, before going to the Gate of Death, she told him that if she did not return he would become the 78th Director. He answered that her work was far from done and reminded her of the rest of her grandfather's saying: "Follow your heart, and do what you can." She asked him to return the Traveler's Rex coin so that, if she died, they would not find it in the debris and blame themselves. He saw that she was trying to cut her worldly attachments, and later told the Traveler how to reach her.

1.content:
Soon after meeting the zombie Qiqi, Hu Tao decided that as her self-proclaimed true friend she should grant her eternal peace. She kidnapped Qiqi several times, each time calculating an auspicious hour and planning a proper cremation and tomb. Each time Baizhu arrived to find Qiqi stuffed in a bag with only her head poking out, watching Hu Tao dig a pit for the pyre. Hu Tao sent a letter apologising for not laying her to rest fast enough. Qiqi learned to remember hiding places just to escape her. Moved by Qiqi's will to live and her history, Hu Tao decided she was a rare exception to the natural order, and began to pamper her. Qiqi still calls her "Warm. Fake smile. Death." and says she despises her.

In 5.3 Qiqi entered the border and was trapped there with Hu Tao and Lan Yan. Hu Tao kept her awake against the fetor with an improvised rhyme about burying her "deep underground". Later she gave Qiqi a "safe passage" fortune coin, joking that she can't bury Qiqi if she doesn't know where she is.

2.content:
The owner of Bubu Pharmacy grew more set on achieving eternal life after meeting Qiqi, and Hu Tao finds that unacceptable. "Baizhu? Ugh, that guy..." Yet the pharmacy and the parlor are neighbours: when a life-and-death question cannot be settled in a few words, she invites him to dinner, and he comes. Over years of shared banquets they have become close friends who keep secrets from each other. Patients who die in his care are sent to a secluded cottage where Wangsheng's consultant performs the rites. Baizhu says he bears her no ill will and that she is the more wary one.

In Baizhu's Story Quest (3.6) she insisted on giving last rites to his dying patient Jialiang, only for Baizhu to save him. His late master was her grandfather's younger brother, once a Wangsheng deputy director, who left to study medicine. At the 5.3 Lantern Rite she gave him a fortune coin with the wish that patients be cured before reaching his door, and declined to wish success to his immortality research. He silently transferred some of his life force to her before the ritual.

3.comment: Hu Tao: Xingqiu, Chongyun and Xiangling
3.content:
Xingqiu came to Wangsheng on an auspicious day with a gift to meet the poet behind the Hilitune. His classical verse met her strange, catchy, chaotic verse, and she "beat the old master with untrained fists". They have composed paired verses ever since, one strict and one playful, with Chongyun dragged in as umpire. Xingqiu thinks one must ask what she is really after. Chongyun respects the parlor but boils at her cheeky "It's nothing you exorcists need to worry about" smile; she marvels at his pure yang. Xiangling is her favourite person to scare. Hu Tao keeps it in check in case Guoba toasts her, and pays her back with fermented plum blossoms and rare ingredients.

The four meet at Third-Round Knockout and roam together. In 6.3 they spent a night on Chiwang Terrace waiting for the moon to be "eaten" and missed the eclipse when they gave up. In 5.3 Hu Tao commissioned an outfit for Xiangling from Chiori and gave all three fortune coins.

4.comment: Hu Tao: The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and the Border
4.content:
Liyue's funeral house, run by the Hu Family for 77 generations. Its philosophy is that everyone deserves a dignified send-off whatever their wealth or standing, and that services are tailored to each client's wishes, whether quiet, lively or lavish. "The living give us Mora to see the dead on their way. We have a responsibility to both parties." It also keeps the secrets of the "border", a boundary world between life and death reached beyond Wuwang Hill, where Ley Lines go haywire and lingering spirits gather. Wangsheng escorts souls with unfinished business across.

Hu Tao told the Traveler the parlor began as a kind of doctor's office. In the Archon War, plague born of the Yakshas' karmic debt and of fallen gods' remains spread through corpses; the founders stopped it by burning the dead and purifying the air, keeping life and death in balance. She describes the border as an old house needing repairs every few centuries or decades. If it fails, souls pour out and death encroaches on the living, as happened millennia ago.

5.content:
Hu Tao met the Traveler and Paimon on Wuwang Hill and roped them into her business plans, assuming they were adventurers. Together they helped Meng's friend Big G pass on peacefully. At the border she asked the spirits about the Traveler's lost sibling; none had seen them, and she promised to keep looking. She invites the Traveler for tea, night walks and ghost-spotting, and teases them freely ("I'm so happy I could die! You're such a fantastic friend!").

In 5.3 she gave the Traveler a branch from her own plum tree "for whenever you miss me". She sent back their Rex coin so its protection would go with them on their dangerous journey. The Traveler, unrecorded by the Ley Lines, reached into the border, took the fetor in her place, and collapsed; she carried them back to the harbor. At dawn she called them "my hero", chided them for being reckless, and composed a poem about receiving the gift of life anew.

6.comment: Hu Tao: Old Hu and Hu Tao's Father
6.content: Old Hu, the 75th Director, was a big, muscular, plain-spoken man who lived without regrets and taught Hu Tao "Live in life, die in death. Follow your heart, do what you can." His son, the 76th Director and the family's best spellcaster in generations, was hosting rituals alone at eight. About a dozen years before the present, the two used the Art of Homa against a fetor surge at Wuwang Hill. The son hesitated, unable to let go of his family, and died instantly. Most of the village was lost and the hill was permanently changed. Old Hu cleaned up the disaster but was weakened and died before sixty. Hu Tao keeps her father's photograph, the one possession of his she could not dismiss. When Ningguang asked in 5.3 whether the border crisis was linked to the disaster, Hu Tao said no and changed the subject. She told the Traveler the whole story when they asked.

7.comment: Hu Tao: Springtime Charms and the Gate of Death
7.content: During the 5.3 Lantern Rite (a limited-time event), fetor leaking from a failing border stole vitality from the elderly in Qingce, Yilong Wharf and Liyue Harbor. Hu Tao reported it to the Ministry of Civil Affairs, went in to investigate and was trapped with Lan Yan and Qiqi until the Traveler and Xiao got them out. She proposed redoing the damaged section of the border by spreading the Art of Homa across the Ley Lines through the Seven-and-Eight-Gates array. Ningguang found the gates; Keqing, Ganyu, Beidou, Yelan, Xiao, Baizhu and Qiqi, and Ningguang with Lan Yan took the others. Hu Tao took the Gate of Death at Wuwang Hill and the obfuscation role, erasing herself from the Ley Lines to seal it. She told everyone this need not mean death, while privately settling her affairs.

8.comment: Hu Tao: The Vision and the Hat
8.content: Her Pyro Vision appeared in her travel bag after she returned, aged thirteen, from waiting at the border for her grandfather's spirit. The story suggests that her daring moved "some unknown god". She is famously indifferent to it. Her hat, the Harmony Hexagram Hat, came from Old Hu and was refitted by hand. It bears the Wangsheng insignia and plum blossoms from a tree she grew herself; she treasures it and keeps it spotless.

key: Lone Butterfly of the Crimson Flame
9.comment: Hu Tao: Staff of Homa and the Eight Adepts
9.content: The Staff of Homa is a ceremonial "firewood staff" handed down the Hu Family, and Hu Tao is its current owner. Its legend tells of a merciful doctor who heard a whisper in the flame, "Only an unbound flame can purify this world", and burned the evil miasma of dead gods. The dead were reduced to ashen butterflies, and the doctor at last became smoke in the shape of a butterfly. Wangsheng's arts descend from the Eight Adepts, who purified the god Tao Dou. The Lone Butterfly of the Crimson Flame gave her life for it, and the Wuwang Kid, who idolised her, passed her techniques on to the parlor. Hu Tao insists those two were the greatest of the Eight.

10.comment: Hu Tao: Meng and Big G
10.content: Hu Tao's Story Quest (1.3). Her new intern Meng joined Wangsheng to find his late childhood friend Big G, whom he feared had become a vengeful spirit. Hu Tao tried to sell Lan of the Adventurers' Guild on a partnership and failed. She checked Meng's old friends for traces of the ghost and staged a fake exorcism for Luocheng, who thought himself cursed. She used a Ley Line Monolith to lure monsters, then told him he likely had a common cold. The monolith also drew in Big G, a small, lost and harmless spirit. With keepsakes from his friends she led everyone into the border, where Meng and Big G said goodbye. She then gave Meng unpaid time off.

11.content: Lan Yan, a craftswoman with a little Qimen art, met Hu Tao during the 5.3 border crisis and was trapped with her. She saw that Hu Tao kept her plans to herself, and she found a way to link rattan figures to every gate so the fetor would be shared. Lan Yan says she hopes Hu Tao's smiles are now genuine rather than meant to reassure. Hu Tao says Lan Yan is stronger than she looks, though curing everyone "isn't exactly good for the funeral business".
